prose: A post on the 'expensive-loop problem' in AI research agents: an agent picks experiments without weighing expected information gain against compute cost, treating a 15-hour multi-GPU run as no more consequential than a 30-minute ablation. The diagnosed root cause is that the agent has no model of information gain relative to cost and no prior on how severe a proposed change is. The piece also quotes a Borges-style parable of a map the size of the empire. Basis: the opening of the post.
highlights: Agents treat a 15-hour run like a 30-minute ablation.
Root cause: no model of information gain versus compute cost.
No prior over consequence severity for proposed changes.
